mechanism_narrative: Residential mobility has increased monotonically from +10.3% to +24.3% over four weeks, indicating sustained lockdown compliance and indoor confinement. This trend will reverse as restrictions ease, releasing pent-up demand for retail-and-recreation visits over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from +10.3% to +24.3% across four consecutive weeks
regime_hint: tightening restrictions transitioning to early reopening
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the prior 28-day mean by at least 5 percentage points when RESIDENTIAL remains above +20% for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has collapsed to -73.6%, indicating near-total cessation of public transport use. This extreme suppression will persist or deepen over the next four weeks, preventing commuter-driven retail access and keeping RETAIL_REC depressed below current levels.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -70% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from -41.3% to -73.6% in four weeks
regime_hint: strict lockdown with public transport restrictions
failure_condition: TRANSIT recovers above -50% within the next two weeks and RETAIL_REC subsequently rises by more than 10 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has declined from +8.0% to -22.1%, signaling tightened restrictions on non-essential retail. This policy-driven suppression of essential-goods mobility will extend to retail-and-recreation, which will remain depressed as restrictions remain in force.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below -15% for one week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM shifted from +8.0% to -22.1% over four weeks
regime_hint: tightening restrictions on all retail categories
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM recovers above -10% within one week and RETAIL_REC does not follow within two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has fallen to -56.3%, indicating near-total workplace closure. When WORKPLACES begins recovery, commuter foot traffic will resume, creating secondary demand for retail-and-recreation venues near transit corridors and employment centers, driving RETAIL_REC upward over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by more than 10 percentage points week-on-week
failure_condition: WORKPLACES rises above -40% and TRANSIT remains below -60% for two consecutive weeks, with RETAIL_REC failing to rise above the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has collapsed from -26.4% to -42.6%, indicating suppressed outdoor recreation. As restrictions ease, PARKS will recover first (outdoor venues open earlier), and this recovery will signal broader reopening that lifts RETAIL_REC within one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above -30% for one week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS declined from -26.4% to -42.6% over four weeks
regime_hint: transition from strict lockdown to phased reopening
failure_condition: PARKS recovers above -25% and RETAIL_REC does not rise within two weeks, or PARKS recovery is followed by a decline below -35% within one week.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC are jointly suppressed by the same policy regime. When GROCERY_PHARM stabilizes or begins recovery, it signals that restrictions on retail access are easing, and RETAIL_REC will follow with a one-to-two-week lag as consumer confidence rebuilds.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM week-on-week change is positive for one week
evidence_refs: fact:Both series declined sharply over four weeks
regime_hint: policy-driven retail restrictions with phased easing
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM rises above -15% for one week and RETAIL_REC does not rise above the prior 28-day mean within two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The snapshot spans mid-April in Victoria during strict lockdown. Seasonal demand for retail-and-recreation (autumn in Southern Hemisphere) is suppressed by policy, not by seasonal factors. As restrictions ease in late April, seasonal demand will reassert, driving RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks independent of other mobility signals.
evidence_refs: fact:Decision date is 2020-04-15, mid-autumn in Victoria
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the prior 28-day mean when RESIDENTIAL remains elevated above +20%.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT, WORKPLACES, and RETAIL_REC form a coupled system: transit collapse prevents workplace commuting, which eliminates retail foot traffic. Recovery requires simultaneous improvement in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES. If either remains suppressed below -50%, RETAIL_REC will not recover over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain below -50% for two consecutive weeks
regime_hint: strict lockdown with transport and workplace closures
failure_condition: Either TRANSIT or WORKPLACES rises above -40% within two weeks and RETAIL_REC does not follow with a rise above the prior 28-day mean within four weeks.
